The '''2022 Hartlepool Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022 to elect members of [[Hartlepool Borough Council]]. This was on the same day as [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections]]. 13 of the 36 seats were up for election, with 1 ward (Rural West) electing 2 councillors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Election timetable in England |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/election-timetable-in-england/election-timetable-in-england#district-councils5 |website=GOV.UK |access-date=17 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==
Hartlepool is traditionally a [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] council, with Labour forming the majority party for most of its history. The council fell into [[no overall control]] from 1976 to 1979, [[2000 Hartlepool Borough Council election|2000]] to 2004, 2008 to 2010, and from [[2019 Hartlepool Borough Council election|2019]] to the present.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hartlepool Borough Council Election Results 1973-1994 |url=http://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Hartlepool-1973-1994.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=23 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hartlepool Borough Council Election Results 1995-2012 |url=http://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Hartlepool-1995-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=23 April 2022}}</ref> A coalition of [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]], [[Independent Union (political party)|Independent Union]], and [[Veterans and People's Party]] councillors took control of the council in 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Minting |first1=Stuart |last2=Metcalfe |first2=Alex |title=Allegiances turned on their head at Ben Houchen's top table |url=https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/news/teesside-news/allegiances-turned-head-ben-houchens-16256905 |access-date=23 April 2022 |work=TeessideLive |date=10 May 2019 |language=en}}</ref> IU and VPP councillors left their parties to join the [[Brexit Party]] in September 2019,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Scott |first1=Jim |title=The Brexit Party take over North-East council |url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/17900531.brexit-party-takes-hold-hartlepool-borough-council/ |access-date=23 April 2022 |work=The Northern Echo |date=13 September 2019 |language=en}}</ref> but most rejoined their original parties in early 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hartlepool Council no longer under Brexit Party control |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-tees-51400045 |access-date=23 April 2022 |work=BBC News |date=6 February 2020}}</ref>

In the [[2021 Hartlepool Borough Council election|2021 election]], which was under new boundaries, the Conservatives won 13 seats with 25.75%, Labour won 11 with 30.70%, [[Independent politician|independents]] won 10 with 25.55%, and the Independent Union won 2 with 6.27%. Separately, the Conservatives won the [[2021 Hartlepool by-election]] on the same day, taking the seat for the first time.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2021-05-07|title=Elections 2021: Conservatives hail historic Labour defeat in Hartlepool by-election|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-57019456|access-date=2022-01-22}}</ref>

* February 2022: Brenda Loynes (Conservative) dies; seat left vacant until 2022 election<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bilalova |first1=Pamela |title=Tributes to 'the most amazing public servant' after Hartlepool Mayor Brenda Loynes's death is announced |url=https://www.hartlepoolmail.co.uk/news/people/tributes-to-hartlepool-mayor-brenda-loynes-after-her-death-is-announced-3559850 |access-date=23 April 2022 |work=Hartlepool Mail |date=8 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
* Sue Little and Leisa Smith join Putting Seaton First from independent
